{{Short description|Abstract algebra subgroup}}
In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[group theory]], a [[subgroup]] of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] is said to be '''descendant''' if there is a descending series starting from the subgroup and ending at the group, such that every term in the series is a [[normal subgroup]] of its predecessor.

The series may be infinite. If the series is finite, then the subgroup is [[subnormal subgroup|subnormal]].
